newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Formosa units jump on bullish profit report.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Formosa units jump on bullish profit report.

text.p: Shares of units of Taiwan's top industrial conglomerate, Formosa Plastics, jumped at mid-morning on Monday, fuelled by a bank's projection of rise in profits after a new petrochemical plant opens in 1999, brokers said.
With 80 minutes to go, three key members -- Formosa Plastics, Nan Ya Plastics and Formosa Chemical and Fiber -- all were higher on active buying.

Formosa Chemical and Fiber was the session's most active issue, surging T$2.3 or 6.46 percent to T$37.9. Formosa Plastics gained T$2 or 3.25 percent to T$63.5 and Nan Ya Plastics advanced T$2 or 3.88 percent to T$53.5.
The Formosa surge triggered a 3.33 percent rise for the entire plastics and chemical sector.

The China Times newspaper quoted an unofficial Mitsubishi Bank study as predicting that profits for the three firms would soar in 2000 after the US$9.0 billion petrochemical project in central Taiwan starts production in 1999.
Formosa group launched the sixth naphtha cracker project in 1993. Construction of the complex, including a naphtha cracker and oil refinery, will take six years to complete.
"Quite a few investors are delighted to see the report and they feel bullish," said Albert Lin, an analyst at Golden Securities. -- Taipei Newsroom (2-5080815)
